_why: Role track for the FITTER, authored under docs/profiling/role-pack-authoring-guide.md as Batch 2 part two's second pack. fam_fitting stays the generic ISCO-unit-7233 interview and is NOT touched; this pack belongs to fam_fitter, which binds the NCO fitting occupations directly (job_domain specificity 50 beats unit 40), so a bench, assembly or plant fitter gets fitting depth and every other worker under 7233 -- the diesel mechanic, the pump mechanic, the loco and marine fitters -- keeps the interview they have today.
_scope: BENCH, ASSEMBLY, MAINTENANCE AND ERECTION FITTING on rotating plant -- gearboxes, pumps, conveyors and hydraulic power packs -- which is the range the reference page shows inside the one word 'fitter'. fitter_work_type is asked of everyone rather than used as a router, because the page's own worker does all three and the ITI trade name does not say which. The level ladder (Helper / Fitter / Senior Fitter) is asked as fitter_level so the sheet can say which rung the man stands on; RoleFormDescriptor.levelLadder is the list it offers. Engine, vehicle and pump MECHANICS are not bound here and are not asked about.
_depth: THE TIER GATE IS fitting_experience, asked FIRST, and it is FITTER.tenureQuestionKey. It cannot be experience_years from qp_universal: phase order runs occupation_specific BEFORE universal_tail, so the universal answer does not exist yet when these items are selected -- gating on it is permanently false. Its options carry value_number ONLY. pack-registry.service.ts resolves valueText ?? valueNumber, so a value_text beside the number would turn every gte gate below into a string comparison that is false forever.
_budget: MAX_ENGINE_ASKS is 48 and qp_universal@4 spends at most 18. Tier 0 is 7 items, tier 1 (fitting_experience >= 2) adds 3, tier 2 (>= 5) adds 3 -- a senior walks 13, two fewer than the welder's 15. The three fresher items are gated fitting_experience <= 0, so a senior never sees them and a fresher, who fails both gte gates by construction, tops out at 7 + 3 = 10. 16 items, none duplicating a qp_universal key.
_sheet: SECTION B IS READ OFF THE RATIFIED FITTER REFERENCE RESUME (Suresh Pawar, page 8), not invented. Its seven rows are Fitting type, Equipment worked on, Bench & assembly work, Tools & instruments, Drawings, Alignment held and Sector worked, and every one has a question here that fills it. Bench & assembly work and Tools & instruments each carry SEVEN options because the page prints seven in each; trimming to the chip guideline's six would have dropped a row value the page shows. fitter_work_type adds 'Bench fitting' beside the page's three because jd_nco_7233_0200 'Fitter, Bench' is bound to this family and its worker would otherwise have no chip. Alignment held is a BANDED single_select, the welder's plate ruling: the page prints 'Coupling alignment to 0.05 mm', which is a band, and a typed number would not render as one. The page prints Bench & assembly work like the sheet metal page's Operations and Tools & instruments like its Measuring instruments, so the first is a chip row and the second a tick row -- read off the layout's parallel, since the extracted text cannot show a tick. The four depth items -- fitter_hydraulic_work (tier 1), fitter_overhaul, fitter_erection and fitter_fault_finding (tier 2) -- have NO sheet row -- the ratified page has none and this pack does not invent one; they are matching data in worker_attributes. This pack has no case in role-sheet-parity.render.test.ts yet.
_keys: NO DIGITS IN ANY question_key OR option_key. Both regexes are ^[a-z_]+$, and slugKey REFUSES a key with a digit at runtime even where the corpus validator historically let it through -- one such key makes the whole pack unparseable. So the alignment bands are point_one / point_zero_five / point_zero_two; the LABEL keeps the real figure ('0.05 mm tak'). measuring_tools, drawing_reading and sector_worked are the SHARED keys other packs already use, deliberately: resume-degradation.ts sheds rows BY KEY (sector_worked first) to keep a sheet on one page, and a private key would opt this trade out of that. measuring_tools carries the page's whole 'Tools & instruments' row -- four instruments and three fitting tools -- because the page prints them as one row in the instruments slot. The work-type key is fitter_work_type and NOT fitting_type: qp_fitting@1 already owns fitting_type with a different vocabulary (bench / maintenance / pipe / assembly), and one key with two vocabularies would let an answer captured under one pack print through the other's dictionary.
review_note: Drafted for owner review. Shop-floor vocabulary NOT yet corrected by a practising fitter -- see docs/registers/trade-content-ratification.md.
_fresher: Guideline section 11 #1: a fresher's Zone 4 is training, trade test, machines used in the ITI workshop and project work, and the History heading never renders empty. These three items are the ask half; resume-fresher-rows.ts, fed by this role's descriptor, is the render half. The KEYS are read literally by that file and must not be renamed; only the workshop VOCABULARY is trade-specific, and an ITI Fitter trainee spends his first year at the bench and vice, so that leads. The three prompts are the welder's verbatim, so they reuse its served text and its voice clips.

items.retry_text: Assembly, maintenance ya erection, kaunsi fitting karte hain?

items.prompt_text: Aap khud ko kis level ka fitter maante hain?
items.why_text: Level se employer ko aapka darja saaf pata chalta hai.

items.prompt_text: Naap aur fitting ke liye kaunse aujaar istemaal karte hain?

items.prompt_text: Kya aap drawing padh lete hain?
